paper.title_en: Self-correcting qubit in a strongly driven LC resonator
paper.abstract_en: We propose a device to realize quantum error correction by dissipation. The device generates Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states as steady states in a single driven LC resonator. The resonator should have impedance above $h/2e^2\approx 12.9\,{\rm k}Ω$, and should be driven across a Josephson junction with a high-amplitude voltage tone at frequency near-commensurate with the resonator frequency. In this regime, we show that GKP states emerge as steady-states of the resonator; these states encode a qubit protected against phase-space local noise. Low-lying excitations preserve the quantum information and increase the energy proportionally to a measure of the error degree. Thus, quantum error correction of both bit and phase errors can be achieved with dissipative cooling. Our calculations indicate an achievable coherence time of $ 1000 \times$ the resonator photon lifetime at operating temperatures above $100 \, {\rm mK}$. Beyond steady-state quantum error correction, the device supports protected single-qubit Clifford gates and readout with exponential accuracy corrected by the same dissipative mechanism, as well as magic-state preparation above the distillation threshold.
